- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are trending downward, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–2% to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after a dip, forecast should be adjusted upward 1–2 days early, not waiting for price confirmation.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth out extreme peaks and troughs by applying a 3-point moving average filter to forecast path.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 7-day mean to anchor forecast.
